# Mentally Healthy Schools

> A comprehensive, DfE-funded resource hub providing evidence-based mental health guidance, toolkits, and whole-school approaches for UK schools and colleges in partnership with Anna Freud and Young Minds.

Mentally Healthy Schools supports school leaders, mental health leads, and staff across primary and secondary settings with practical resources covering neurodiversity, targeted interventions, attendance, and mental wellbeing. The platform combines whole-school frameworks with specific guidance on anxiety, depression, peer pressure, and other key mental health topics affecting children and young people.

## Key Topics

- Mental health support
- Whole-school approach
- School resources
- Neurodiversity (ADHD, autism)
- Protective factors
- Risk factors
- Early intervention
- Safeguarding
- School staff guidance
- Wellbeing
- Targeted support
- Vulnerable children
- CAMHS referral
- Child wellbeing
- Lifestyle factors

## Core Resources & Hubs

- [Home](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk): Homepage covering mental health resources across UK schools
- [Resource hub](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/resources): Main resource hub with toolkits for ADHD, autism, neurodiversity support
- [Mental health lead resource hub](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/whole-school-or-college-resources): DfE-funded resource hub for school leaders and mental health leads
- [Targeted support hub](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/targeted-support-hub): Hub of evidence-based targeted interventions for schools and colleges

## Whole-School Approaches

- [Whole-school approach](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/whole-school-approach): Framework for whole-school mental health with staff and parent engagement
- [Targeted support](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/targeted-support): DfE-funded guidance for graduated response and intervention planning
- [Attendance and mental wellbeing in schools and colleges](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/attendance-and-mental-wellbeing-school-college): Resources addressing attendance barriers and mental wellbeing support

## Mental Health Information & Topics

- [Mental health information](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/mental-health-information): Overview of risk and protective factors in child mental health
- [Anxiety](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/mental-health-information/anxiety-redirect): Anxiety guidance with animation toolkit and teacher resources
- [Low mood or depression](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/mental-health-information/low-mood-or-depression-redirect): Depression identification and CAMHS referral guidance for staff
- [Neurodiversity](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/mental-health-information/neurodiversity-redirect): Neurodiversity support for ADHD, autism, dysgraphia in schools
- [Peer pressure](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/mental-health-information/peer-pressure-redirect): Peer pressure, bullying, and social media impact on wellbeing
- [Body image](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/mental-health-information/body-image-redirect): Body image, self-esteem, and adolescent health guidance
- [Mental health information topics](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/mental-health-information/see-more-topics): Index page linking to additional mental health topics

## Getting Started Guides

- [Primary](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/getting-started/primary): Getting started guide for primary schools with early intervention focus
- [Secondary](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/getting-started/secondary): Getting started guide for secondary schools with adolescent focus

## About & Support

- [About](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/about): Organization background and mission with Anna Freud and Young Minds partnerships
- [Concerned about a child or young person?](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/concerned-about-a-child-or-young-person): Crisis guidance with helpline resources: NSPCC, Childline, GP, A&E

## Optional

- [Website feedback](https://mentallyhealthyschools.org.uk/website-feedback): User feedback form for website usability and improvement
